policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 18:2 reads 'And he called to him a little child' with a pronoun subject; the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς would have produced a named subject, as ASV renders elsewhere. The English distinguishes the shorter text.
ἐὰν and ἂν in the relative clause are orthographic variants of the same particle; 'whoso shall receive' renders either. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
The three readings differ only in the accusative form of τοιοῦτο(ν) and in word order; 'one such little child' renders all three identically. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.

Both readings are prepositions of attachment at the same slot, and ASV 'hanged about his neck' renders either; nothing else in the verse shifts with the choice. The greek_gloss note concerns the millstone, not this unit.
The added ἐστιν is the copula of the impersonal ἀνάγκη; ASV 'for it must needs be' supplies the verb of being either way. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.

ASV 'that man through whom the occasion cometh' can render the anaphoric article with its relative clause as readily as ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ; the English demonstrative is idiomatic for both readings and no mapped note bears on the unit.

ASV 18:8 'cut it off, and cast it from thee' is singular, answering the singular αὐτὸν; the plural αὐτὰ would have given 'cast them from thee' for the two members named. The English number distinguishes.
ASV 18:8 'to enter into life maimed or halt' follows the order κυλλὸν ἢ χωλόν; the transposed reading would have given 'halt or maimed'. The order of the paired adjectives is visible in the English.

ASV ends 18:10 at 'my Father who is in heaven' and prints no verse 11 in the text, passing from 18:10 to 18:12; the long reading would have supplied that sentence. The absence of the clause from the ASV text distinguishes the shorter reading.

ASV 'doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and go unto the mountains, and seek' renders a coordinated participle as readily as a finite verb; English regularly resolves ἀφεὶς into a finite 'leave'. No mapped note bears on the unit — the 18:12 textual_variant note concerns the inserted verse 11.

The 'and' before 'go unto the mountains' is the coordination English supplies for a following participle whether or not καὶ stands in the Greek. The mapped textual_variant note here concerns the inserted verse 11, not this connective.

The ASV note mapped to 18:14, 'Greek a thing willed before your Father,' renders ἔμπροσθεν with 'before'; the omitting reading leaves nothing for that word. The note distinguishes the reading that retains ἔμπροσθεν.
ASV text reads 'your Father who is in heaven' and the mapped textual_variant note, 'Some ancient authorities read my,' places μου in the margin. The text renders ὑμῶν.
ἓν and εἷς differ only in gender agreement; 'that one of these little ones should perish' renders either. The mapped note at 18:14 concerns 'your' for 'my', not this unit.
ASV text reads 'if thy brother sin against thee' and the mapped textual_variant note, 'Some ancient authorities omit against thee,' assigns the omission to the margin. The text renders εἰς σὲ.

ASV 18:15 reads 'go, show him his fault' with asyndeton, where the added καὶ would give 'go and show him'. ASV renders καί in such imperative pairs, so the absent conjunction distinguishes the shorter reading.
ἐὰν and ἂν are orthographic variants of the same particle after the relative; 'what things soever ye shall bind' renders either. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
The added article before οὐρανῷ is not rendered in English: ASV has 'in heaven' for the arthrous and anarthrous alike. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
As at the first occurrence in the verse, the added article before οὐρανῷ leaves 'in heaven' unchanged in English. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
ASV 18:19 begins 'Again I say unto you' with no 'Verily', though ASV renders ἀμήν as 'Verily' in the immediately preceding 18:18. The absent adverb distinguishes the reading that omits ἀμήν.
The readings differ in word order and in whether the partitive is ἐξ ὑμῶν or bare ὑμῶν; ASV 'if two of you shall agree' renders both. The greek_gloss note concerns 'shall become', not this unit.
The readings differ only in the position of αὐτῷ relative to ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν; ASV 'Then came Peter and said to him' fixes the English order regardless. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
προσηνέχθη and προσήχθη are aorist passives of near-synonymous compounds, both rendered 'was brought'. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes; the note on the talent bears on the sum.
The readings differ only in the order of αὐτῷ and εἷς; ASV 'one was brought unto him' renders either. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.

ASV 'his lord commanded him to be sold' renders the possessive article of ὁ κύριος as naturally as ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ; English supplies 'his' for the master of the parable either way. No mapped note bears on the unit.
ASV 'and his wife, and children' takes the article of τὴν γυναῖκα possessively as readily as it renders γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
ἔχει and εἶχεν differ in tense within a clause English puts into the past by sequence anyway: 'all that he had' renders both. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
ASV 18:26 reads 'saying, Lord, have patience with me'; the vocative 'Lord' has no counterpart in the reading that begins at Μακροθύμησον. The vocative in the English distinguishes the longer reading.
ἐμοί and ἐμέ differ only in the case governed by ἐπί; ASV 'have patience with me' renders either. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
The readings differ only in the order of ἀποδώσω and σοι; ASV 'I will pay thee all' fixes the English order regardless. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
ASV 18:28 reads 'Pay what thou owest' with no indirect object; the added μοι would give 'Pay me that thou owest'. The absent 'me' distinguishes the shorter reading.
ASV 18:29 reads 'fell down and besought him' with nothing answering εἰς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ, which would give 'fell down at his feet'. The absent phrase distinguishes the shorter reading.
As in 18:26, ἐμοί and ἐμέ differ only in the case governed by ἐπί; 'Have patience with me' renders either. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
ἕως οὗ and bare ἕως are alternative forms of the same temporal conjunction; ASV 'till he should pay' renders either. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
ASV opens 18:31 with 'So when his fellow-servants saw', a resumptive 'So' that renders the narrative δὲ as readily as οὖν. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.
ASV 18:34 reads 'till he should pay all that was due', with nothing answering αὐτῷ, which would give 'all that was due unto him'. The absent dative distinguishes the shorter reading.
οὐράνιος and ἐπουράνιος are both rendered 'heavenly' in ASV usage; 'my heavenly Father' renders either. No ASV wording or mapped note distinguishes.

ASV 18:35 ends 'if ye forgive not every one his brother from your hearts', with nothing answering τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, which would add 'their trespasses'. The absent object distinguishes the shorter reading.
